#### What type of PR is this?
/kind bug

<!--
Add one of the following kinds:

Optionally add one or more of the following kinds if applicable:

/kind regression
-->

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
1. Adds staticcheck to hack/verify-golangci-lint.sh
2. Fixes or ignores staticcheck failures
3. Removes hack/verify-staticcheck.sh and cleans up hack/tools/go.mod

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
<!--
*Automatically closes linked issue when PR is merged.
Usage: `Fixes #<issue number>`, or `Fixes (paste link of issue)`.
_If PR is about `failing-tests or flakes`, please post the related issues/tests in a comment and do not use `Fixes`_*
-->
Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/103721

#### Special notes for your reviewer:
There were a lot of failures for SA5011 "possible nil pointer dereference".  The original issue showed 3 occurrences, but after I fixed those with `//nolint:staticcheck`, I found that more showed up the next time I ran the lint check. All of the occurrences of this failure happened on something of the following form:
```
		rs, err := rc.clientSet.AppsV1().ReplicaSets(rc.nsName).Get(context.TODO(), rc.name, metav1.GetOptions{})
		framework.ExpectNoError(err)
		if rs == nil {
			framework.Failf(rsIsNil)
		}
		return int(rs.Status.ReadyReplicas)
```

The linter says that:
```
test/e2e/framework/autoscaling/autoscaling_utils.go:340:17: SA5011: possible nil pointer dereference (staticcheck)
		return int(rs.Status.ReadyReplicas)
		              ^
test/e2e/framework/autoscaling/autoscaling_utils.go:337:6: SA5011(related information): this check suggests that the pointer can be nil (staticcheck)
		if rs == nil {
		   ^
```

I read [here](https://staticcheck.io/docs/checks#SA5011) that the linter is unable to detect that our `framework.Failf()` function results in a panic further down the call chain, which causes the linter to flag all of these cases as a violation of SA5011. The proposed solution from that link is to add a `panic("unreachable")` to `framework.Failf()` so that the linter will understand that a panic occurs, so I did that and it fixed all of the errors except for two. Those two used `Skipf` instead of `Failf`, so I added the `panic("unreachable")` to `Skipf` as well. The other option I thought of was to add `-e SA5011` in hack/verify-golangci-lint.sh but that seemed less ideal because it could hide real errors.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
<!--
If no, just write "NONE" in the release-note block below.
If yes, a release note is required:
Enter your extended release note in the block below. If the PR requires additional action from users switching to the new release, include the string "action required".

For more information on release notes see: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/release-notes.md
-->

```release-note
NONE
```

review_comments: does this mean SA1015 is not running any more?

I removed the `//lint:ignore` comment because I changed line 160 from `time.Tick`, which leaks (according to the description [here](https://pkg.go.dev/time#Tick)), to `time.NewTicker`, which does not leak. I believe SA1015 is still running though, as it is included in the staticcheck [docs](https://staticcheck.io/docs/checks#SA1015).

both would leak if the ticker is not stopped, but i'm assuming that the status manager and this ticker normally have the lifespan of that of the process.

the example here https://pkg.go.dev/time#NewTicker shows how the object should be managed properly. notice the `defer ..Stop()`.

Ah yes you're right. I could add a `defer syncTicker.Stop()` inside that goroutine at line 162 but I'm not sure if that's worth it since the for select loop will run forever anyway, and because as you and the previous //lint:ignore comment both said, the ticker is only created once.

process lifespan memory leaks can still show up in software that does leak detection...at least for object code from languages without a GC.

the lack of stop can be a problem, if one day the status_manager code is (for some reason) adapted to a dynamic restart but the stop is never added. maybe our static check tools will catch this problem, maybe not.
glad to see this can get dropped... curious if that's because the new static check is more accurate or for some other reason

The staticcheck [docs](https://staticcheck.io/docs/checks#SA5011) say that SA5011 is `A pointer is being dereferenced unconditionally, while also being checked against nil in another place.` So in this particular case, I believe that removing the check for `r != nil` at line 809 makes it so that r is _not_ "also being checked against nil in another place" so SA5011 no longer cares about it.
This suggests a lack of tests, doesn't it?  Can we tag owners on these when we find them?
yeah... I think `Add()` would actually do the right thing on a struct receiver, but `Result()` would not

Yeah, good call about testing. There does appear to be a test [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/cm/cpuset/cpuset_test.go#L24) but I guess it is not comprehensive enough.

is it worth using static check pragmas here instead of panicing?
e.g. ` //nolint:staticcheck`
(same for the one bellow)

I did start by adding the `//nolint:staticcheck` in several places but there ended up being many occurrences of SA5011 (I kept fixing a few and then more would show up the next time I linted; maybe the output was truncated) so I decided that adding the panic would be simpler. Adding the `panic("unreachable")` also appeared to be a recommended approach, from the docs that I linked in the PR description up top, for handling a case where staticcheck doesn't understand that the control flow has been aborted.
